## Mandatory bug structure
**Title**: `[BUG] | [Module] | [Observed behaviour] vs [Expected behaviour]`

**Summary**: One concise paragraph describing the defect

**Environment**:
- Application: (e.g. Staging — staging.client.com)
- Build: (commit hash or version)
- Browser/Device: (e.g. Chrome 124, Windows 11)
- User type: (Guest / Logged-in)
- Locale: (e.g. en-IN)

**Steps to Reproduce**: Numbered steps starting from app entry point

**Expected Result**: What should happen per the AC scenario (reference Jira ID if known)

**Actual Result**: What actually happens — include exact UI text

**Reproducibility**: Always / N of N attempts

**Severity**: Critical / Major / Minor / Trivial (per bug_writing_standards)

| save the draft as Markdown in .astound/ba/drafts using workspace file tools | Save the epic draft for review |

## Purpose

Provide a repeatable approach to choosing Apex test scope for PR vs release, with fast feedback while maintaining safety.

## PR checks (default)

- Run **impacted tests** when:
  - Change is small and localized.
  - No security / sharing model changes.

- Escalate to **`RunLocalTests`** when:

- Always run **`RunLocalTests`** for promotion to UAT / PreProd / Prod.
- Keep a curated **smoke test class list** for critical flows if runtime is a concern.

- When deploying non-Apex changes that fail under `RunSpecifiedTests` because of **unrelated** org-level validation rules or coverage requirements, use `--test-level NoTestRun` and run the affected test classes separately afterwards. Document this in the story's `deployment.md`.

- Store test output as pipeline artifacts.

# Skill: Custom Application + Utility Bar pattern

A small, deploy-tight pattern for delivering a custom Lightning app with a utility bar.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `force-app/main/default/applications/<App>.app-meta.xml` | The CustomApplication: tabs, navType, formFactors, `<utilityBar>` reference |
| `force-app/main/default/flexipages/<App>_UtilityBar.flexipage-meta.xml` | UtilityBar FlexiPage referenced by the app |
| `force-app/main/default/profiles/<Profile>.profile-meta.xml` | `<applicationVisibilities>` for `<App>` (`visible=true`) per profile |

## CustomApplication skeleton

```xml
<CustomApplication ...>
    <label>My App</label>
    <navType>Standard</navType>
    <uiType>Lightning</uiType>
    <formFactors>Large</formFactors>
    <formFactors>Small</formFactors>
    <tabs>standard-home</tabs>
    <tabs>standard-Account</tabs>
    <tabs>standard-Opportunity</tabs>
    <!-- ... ordered list of tabs ... -->
    <utilityBar>My_App_UtilityBar</utilityBar>
</CustomApplication>
```

## Tab API names (common reference)

| UI label | Tab API name |
|---|---|
| Home | `standard-home` |
| Accounts | `standard-Account` |
| Contacts | `standard-Contact` |
| Leads | `standard-Lead` |
| Opportunities | `standard-Opportunity` |
| Campaigns | `standard-Campaign` |
| Campaign Members | `standard-Campaign` (no separate member tab in most orgs) |
| Products | `standard-Product2` |
| Quotes | `standard-Quote` |
| Reports | `standard-report` |
| Dashboards | `standard-Dashboard` |
| Tasks | `standard-Task` |
| Calendar | `standard-Event` |
| Forecasts | `standard-Forecasting3` |

For a custom-object tab, use `<Namespace>__<Object>__c` (e.g. `My_Custom_Object__c`).

For an "all tabs visible" permission-set entry (Sales Operations Advanced Access pattern), iterate `SELECT Name FROM TabDefinition WHERE IsAvailableInAloha = true` for the target org and emit each as a `<tabSettings>` of `Visible`.

## UtilityBar FlexiPage skeleton

```xml
<FlexiPage ...>
    <masterLabel>My App Utility Bar</masterLabel>
    <type>UtilityBar</type>
    <flexiPageRegions>
        <name>utilityItems</name>
        <type>Region</type>
        <itemInstances>
            <componentInstance>
                <componentName>notes:utilityBarNoteList</componentName>
            </componentInstance>
            <componentInstance>
                <componentName>runtime_sales_todo_list:unifiedToDoListAuraWrapper</componentName>
            </componentInstance>
        </itemInstances>
    </flexiPageRegions>
</FlexiPage>
```

## Profile visibility

Add to each profile that should see the app (do not forget Admin):

```xml
<applicationVisibilities>
    <application>My_App</application>
    <default>false</default>
    <visible>true</visible>
</applicationVisibilities>
```

**Always retrieve the full profile (especially `Admin`) before editing**; partial profile files can clobber unrelated permissions.

## Deploy

```bash
sf project deploy start \
  --source-dir force-app/main/default/applications \
  --source-dir force-app/main/default/flexipages \
  --source-dir force-app/main/default/profiles \
  --target-org <alias>
```

## Post-deploy

- Setup -> App Manager -> confirm the app is listed.
- App Launcher -> confirm the app appears for each profile (use **Login As** to check).
- If the app exists but the launcher does not show it for a profile, the profile's `<applicationVisibilities>` `visible` is `false` — re-retrieve, fix, redeploy.

# Skill: Core Logic (Domain Knowledge)

Use this when implementing or reviewing backend and data logic.

## Expertise areas

- **Apex:** Triggers (handler pattern), bulkification, governor limits, order of execution.
- **SOQL / SOSL:** Selective queries, relationship queries, bulk-safe patterns, limits.
- **Salesforce order of execution:** Record-triggered flows vs triggers vs process builders, before / after save, commit order.
- **Async:** Batch, Queueable, Schedulable, Platform Events.

## Key patterns

- One trigger per object -> handler class; no logic in the trigger body beyond delegation.
- Collect IDs in loops; run SOQL / DML once outside loops.
- Use `Security.stripInaccessible()` (or `WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED` in SOQL) before DML; respect sharing and FLS unless explicitly elevated and documented.
- Static `Boolean` flags used for re-entrancy or bypass control must be **explicitly initialized to `false`** — unboxing a null `Boolean` in `if (flag)` causes runtime errors.
- For after-save work that needs to re-run platform features (e.g. assignment rules), use an `@InvocableMethod` callable from a Flow with `Database.DMLOptions.assignmentRuleHeader.useDefaultRule = true`.
- Avoid hardcoding profile names; prefer **Custom Permission** checks via `FeatureManagement.checkPermission('Permission_Api_Name')`.

## Order-of-execution reminders

| Phase | What runs |
|---|---|
| 1 | System validation (required fields, foreign keys, max length) |
| 2 | Before-save record-triggered Flows (fast field updates on `$Record`) |
| 3 | Before triggers (Apex) |
| 4 | Custom validation rules |
| 5 | Save (not committed) |
| 6 | After triggers (Apex) |
| 7 | Assignment rules, auto-response, workflow rules |
| 8 | Process Builder / Workflow field updates -> after-save flows -> after triggers re-fire |
| 9 | Roll-up summary, sharing rules, commit, post-commit (async, email) |

Use this to decide between **before-save flow** (cheap, same record) and **after-save flow / Apex** (cross-object, async, callouts).

# Skill: Custom Metadata-driven configuration

Use this when a business rule, mapping, or eligibility check is likely to change without a code deploy, or when the same engine should evaluate many similar conditions.

## When to use

- **Mapping tables:** source value -> target value, key-tuple -> result (e.g. `(Segment, Sub-Segment, Application Code) -> Application Id`).
- **Eligibility / condition rules:** an expression like `1 AND 2` referencing atomic conditions stored as records.
- **Per-record-type / per-environment defaults** that should not require a code change to update.
- Anything an admin should be able to tune in production without involving an engineer.

## Anti-patterns (when *not* to use)

- A handful of constants that almost never change -> use Apex constants or a custom setting (hierarchical) instead.
- Logic that needs millisecond-fast lookup at very high volume -> consider Custom Settings (cached) or Platform Cache.
- Anything containing secrets or PII -> never. Use Named Credentials / vault.

## Pattern A — Simple key -> value mapping

A single Custom Metadata Type (CMT) where each record carries the source key fields and the result.

| Field on `<Mapping>__mdt` | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `<Key1>__c` | Text | First lookup key |
| `<Key2>__c` | Text | Second lookup key (if composite) |
| `Result__c` | Text / Number | The mapped value |

In a **before-save Flow** on the source object:

1. **Entry filter:** all key fields are populated.
2. **Get Records** on `<Mapping>__mdt` with equality on each key field.
3. **Decision:** if a record was found, set `$Record.<TargetField>` to `Get_Result.Result__c`.

In Apex, query the CMT once outside loops; cache results in a `Map<String, <Mapping>__mdt>` keyed by the composite key.

## Pattern B — Configurable rule engine ("logic + atomic conditions")

Useful when admins need to express "Account Status != Inactive AND Contact Status != Inactive" without changing code. Shape your CMTs as a parent "rule set" with one or more child "atomic conditions."

### Schema (suggested names — adapt to your project)

`<Rule_Logic>__mdt` (parent rule set):

| Field | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `DeveloperName` | (built-in) | Stable key for callers (e.g. `Lead_Conversion`) |
| `Condition_Logic__c` | Text | Boolean expression referencing condition `Order__c`s, e.g. `1 AND 2`, `(1 AND 2) OR 3` |

`<Rule_Condition>__mdt` (atomic conditions):

| Field | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Logic_Link__c` | Metadata Relationship -> `<Rule_Logic>__mdt` | Parent rule set |
| `Order__c` | Number | The slot referenced by `Condition_Logic__c` |
| `Object_Name__c` | Text | API name of the object the condition reads (e.g. `Account`, `Contact`) |
| `Field_API__c` | Text | Field API name on that object (e.g. `Status__c`) |
| `Operator__c` | Picklist | `==`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, `contains`, `startsWith`, `endsWith` |
| `Field_Value__c` | Text | Expected value |

### Apex evaluator (sketch)

- `@AuraEnabled` for LWC, `@InvocableMethod` for Flow.
- Public method `evaluate(String logicDeveloperName, Map<String, SObject> context)`:
  1. Load logic + conditions for the given `logicDeveloperName`.
  2. For each condition, read the field from the relevant context record and apply `Operator__c` against `Field_Value__c` -> Boolean per `Order__c`.
  3. Substitute the booleans into `Condition_Logic__c` and evaluate (a small expression parser, or a constrained set of supported expressions).
  4. Return the final boolean (and optional reasons for false conditions).

### Trigger guard

Pair the evaluator with a `BeforeUpdate` guard (e.g. `LeadConversionGuard`) that calls `evaluate` and `addError` if the result is `false`. Surface the same evaluator to a UI banner LWC so the user sees the warning before they submit.

## Conventions

- CMT API names: `<Domain>_<What>__mdt` (e.g. `Country_Region_Mapping__mdt`).
- Records named with a stable, human-readable `DeveloperName` — sequential (`MAP_0001`, `MAP_0002`, ...) for high-volume mappings or business-meaningful names (`Account_Status_Must_Not_Be_Inactive`) for rule conditions.
- Always document the CMT and its records in `docs/PROJECT_SCHEMA.md`.
- For mapping tables loaded from a CSV / spreadsheet, keep the source file under version control (e.g. `data/<mapping>.csv`) and a regeneration script under `scripts/` listed in `.forceignore` so the CLI does not treat scripts as metadata.

## Deployment

- Deploy the CMT object first, then the records.
- Records are deployed as `<Cmt>.<DeveloperName>.md-meta.xml` files.
- If admins manage the records in production, document in the runbook that the **records** in source are seed values; environments diverge after admin edits.

# Skill: Deployment troubleshooting

Lessons from real deploy incidents. Use when a deploy fails, hangs, or "looks stuck."

## Symptoms and root causes

### Deploy "hangs" or loops

- **Wrong CLI usage.** `--metadata FlexiPage,Layout,Profile` as one joined argument is invalid in modern `sf` and the CLI may never validate components correctly. **Use a manifest** (`--manifest manifest/<story>-package.xml`) or one `--metadata Type:Member` per component.
- **Org queue.** Deploys stay `Pending` until Salesforce processes them; the CLI redraws progress until `--wait` minutes elapse. Use `--wait 15` (or higher) and accept the wait.
- **`RunSpecifiedTests` rollback.** If any specified test fails, Salesforce rolls back the whole deploy and nothing lands in the org. The CLI may keep waiting. Pick the right test level for the change (see below).

### "Whole deploy rolled back" with no clear reason

- A single failing test in `RunSpecifiedTests` (or `RunLocalTests`) rolls back the whole package — even non-Apex changes. Check the test result in Setup -> Deployment Status.
- If the failing test is **unrelated to your change** (e.g. an existing test fails because the org now requires a custom field your story did not touch), use `--test-level NoTestRun` for sandbox validation deploys and run the relevant test class separately afterwards. Document this in the story's `deployment.md`.

### "Unknown user permission" or "permission requires <other>"

- Salesforce enforces permission dependency chains (e.g. `ManageUsers` requires `DelegatedTwoFactor` + `MonitorLoginHistory`; `Modify All` implies `Delete` + `View All`). Add the implied permissions to the permission set / profile. See `.cursor/skills/Profile_PermissionSet_Patterns.md`.
- Some permissions (e.g. `AllowForecasting`, `ExportReports`, `ManageMfaInUserInterface`) are not accepted as `<userPermissions>` in some orgs. Grant them in Setup or via a feature license; do not add them to the bundle.

### "App exists but does not appear in the App Launcher"

- The profile's `<applicationVisibilities>` for the app has `visible=false`, or the profile file in source is partial and clobbered the org default. **Retrieve the full profile, fix `visible=true`, redeploy.** See `.cursor/skills/Profile_PermissionSet_Patterns.md`.

### "Action not visible in the highlights panel" / "Action not on the action bar"

- The FlexiPage `actionInstance` is missing or filtered out -> add / fix the visibility rule.
- The page **layout's** `platformActionList` does not include the qualified `Object.Action` -> add it to every relevant layout.

### "Cannot specify a default on: Opportunity" (and similar)

- Some objects' BusinessProcess metadata does not allow `<default>` on individual stage `<values>` (Opportunity is one). Omit the `<default>` element on each stage; the default is set elsewhere.

### "Field is in source but missing in the org" / picklist value not honored

- Picklist value sets are governed by the **standard value set** (for standard picklists) or by the field metadata (for custom picklists). Update the right place; deploy the value set first if you are renaming or replacing.
- If the org uses Excel/scientific notation in a CSV source (e.g. `4.00E+01`), normalize to the literal value (`04E1`) before generating metadata. Source CSV typos commonly become deployment failures.

## Recipes

### Sandbox deploy that should ignore unrelated test failures

```bash
sf project deploy start \
  --manifest manifest/<story-id>-package.xml \
  --target-org <sandbox-alias> \
  --test-level NoTestRun \
  --ignore-conflicts \
  --wait 15
```

Then run the affected test classes separately:

```bash
sf apex run test \
  --class-names <TouchedTestClass> \
  --result-format human \
  --code-coverage \
  --target-org <sandbox-alias> \
  --wait 10
```

### Production-style deploy

```bash
sf project deploy validate \
  --manifest manifest/<release>-package.xml \
  --target-org <prod-or-staging-alias> \
  --test-level RunLocalTests \
  --wait 60

# After validation succeeds, quick-deploy in your release pipeline.
```

### Retrieve before edit (avoid clobber)

```bash
sf project retrieve start --metadata Profile:Admin --target-org <alias>
sf project retrieve start --metadata FlexiPage:<Name> --target-org <alias>
```

### Diff a single file deploy

```bash
sf project deploy start \
  --source-dir force-app/main/default/objects/<Object>/fields/<Field>.field-meta.xml \
  --target-org <alias>
```

## Pre-deploy checklist (when in doubt)

- [ ] Manifest is up to date and includes all dependent metadata.
- [ ] Dependent objects / fields / record types deploy **before** the components that reference them.
- [ ] Profiles were retrieved (not hand-written) before edit.
- [ ] Permission set dependencies normalized.
- [ ] Test class data satisfies all active validation rules in the target org.
- [ ] Story's `deployment.md` reflects the actual command(s) used.

# Skill: Dynamic Forms and Field Visibility

How to surface fields where you want them seen and lock them down where they should not be edited, using FlexiPages, page layouts, and profile FLS together.

## When to use which lever

| Goal | Use |
|---|---|
| Hide a field from a specific persona | Profile / Permission Set FLS (`readable=false`) |
| Show a field but make it read-only on the record page | Dynamic Forms field on FlexiPage with `uiBehavior=readonly`, plus FLS `editable=false` if it must be read-only everywhere |
| Remove the **Change Record Type** action | `<excludeButtons>ChangeRecordType</excludeButtons>` on the page layout |
| Keep a field readable on Lightning but hide on the layout's Detail tab | Remove from the layout's System Information section; surface via Dynamic Forms field section |

## Pattern A — Read-only field in the record page header

For a field like `RecordType` that the user should see but never change inline:

1. Open the FlexiPage for the record page in App Builder (or edit the `*.flexipage-meta.xml`).
2. Add a Field Section in the **header region** (just under the Highlights Panel).
3. Place the field inside; set `uiBehavior=readonly`.
4. Remove the same field from the **System Information** field section on the Detail tab so it cannot be edited there.

```xml
<itemInstances>
    <fieldInstance>
        <fieldInstanceProperties>
            <name>uiBehavior</name>
            <value>readonly</value>
        </fieldInstanceProperties>
        <fieldItem>Record.RecordTypeId</fieldItem>
        <identifier>fieldRecordTypeReadonly</identifier>
    </fieldInstance>
</itemInstances>
```

## Pattern B — Disable Change Record Type on a page layout

```xml
<platformActionList>
    <actionListContext>Record</actionListContext>
    ...
</platformActionList>
<excludeButtons>ChangeRecordType</excludeButtons>
```

This hides the action from Lightning Experience and the Salesforce Mobile App for layouts where the metadata is applied. Keep it on a separate "admin layout" where Change Record Type should remain available for support work.

## Pattern C — `enablePageActionConfig`

`enablePageActionConfig=true` lets the FlexiPage drive header actions per page. **It requires Dynamic Actions for the object to be enabled** under Setup -> Salesforce Mobile App -> Dynamic Actions. If the org has not enabled it, deploy fails with a not-very-helpful message. Default to `false` unless you have confirmed the setup.

## Pattern D — Action visibility filters in the highlights panel

When you add quick actions to the highlights panel (e.g. an Accept / Reject pair), restrict them with visibility filters so they only appear in the right state:

```xml
<actionInstance>
    <actionName>MyObject.Accept_Action</actionName>
    <visibilityRule>
        <criteria>
            <leftValue>{!Record.Some_Flag__c}</leftValue>
            <operator>EQUAL</operator>
            <rightValue>true</rightValue>
        </criteria>
        <criteria>
            <leftValue>{!Record.Status__c}</leftValue>
            <operator>NE</operator>
            <rightValue>Accepted</rightValue>
        </criteria>
        <criteria>
            <leftValue>{!Record.Status__c}</leftValue>
            <operator>NE</operator>
            <rightValue>Rejected</rightValue>
        </criteria>
    </visibilityRule>
</actionInstance>
```

Two `NE` checks for "anything other than Accepted / Rejected" are equivalent to "status is blank" when the picklist only has those two values; document this in the design note.

## Pattern E — Mirror layout actions across record types

If the same quick action should appear on multiple page layouts (one per record type), add it to the `platformActionList` on each layout file with the qualified `Object.ActionName` form.

## Field Level Security (FLS) — quick reference

| Goal | Profile / PS XML |
|---|---|
| Hidden | `readable=false`, `editable=false` |
| Read-only | `readable=true`, `editable=false` |
| Read + write | `readable=true`, `editable=true` |

Note: a formula field is always read-only; you only set `readable`. FLS for required fields cannot be set to `readable=false`.

# Skill: Email notification on record / owner / queue change

How to deliver a branded, one-shot email notification triggered by a record change (commonly: ownership changes to a specific Queue) without writing Apex.

## Components

| Component | File | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Letterhead | `force-app/main/default/letterhead/<Brand>_Letterhead.letter-meta.xml` | Branded header / footer / colors |
| Email Folder | `force-app/main/default/email/<Folder>-meta.xml` | Folder that holds the template |
| Email Template | `force-app/main/default/email/<Folder>/<Template>.email` + `.email-meta.xml` | The template body and metadata (subject, related entity, letterhead) |
| Record-Triggered Flow | `force-app/main/default/flows/<Object>_<Trigger>.flow-meta.xml` | Detects the change and sends the email |

## Letterhead skeleton

```xml
<Letterhead ...>
    <available>true</available>
    <backgroundColor>#FFFFFF</backgroundColor>
    <bodyColor>#FFFFFF</bodyColor>
    <description>Brand letterhead</description>
    <footer>
        <backgroundColor>#333333</backgroundColor>
        <height>20</height>
    </footer>
    <header>
        <backgroundColor>#0071C5</backgroundColor>
        <height>40</height>
    </header>
    <name>Brand Letterhead</name>
    <topLine>
        <color>#0071C5</color>
        <height>1</height>
    </topLine>
</Letterhead>
```

## Email Template skeleton (text type)

```xml
<EmailTemplate ...>
    <available>true</available>
    <encodingKey>UTF-8</encodingKey>
    <folderName>My_Notifications</folderName>
    <letterhead>Brand_Letterhead</letterhead>
    <name>My Notification</name>
    <relatedEntityType>Lead</relatedEntityType>
    <subject>Regarding your inquiry</subject>
    <type>text</type>
    <uiType>Aloha</uiType>
</EmailTemplate>
```

Body file (`*.email`) uses standard merge fields like `{{{Lead.FirstName}}}`.

## Record-Triggered Flow (after-save)

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Object | Lead (or your object) |
| Trigger Type | Record-Triggered, after save |
| Record Trigger | Create and Update |
| Process Type | AutoLaunchedFlow |
| Status | Active |

### Entry conditions

- `OwnerId` `IsChanged` true (only fires on owner change for updates).
- `Owner:Queue.QueueName` equals `<Target Queue Name>` (this is the trick — use the cross-object reference to read the Queue's name).
- `Email` is not blank (guard against records without an email address).

### Elements

1. **Decision** — `Check_Is_Queue`: confirms the owner is the target Queue and the email is not blank (defensive — entry conditions already cover this; the decision keeps the flow readable).
2. **Action** — Send Email using the email template; recipient is the record's email address.

### Behavior

- **Insert** with the target Queue as owner -> sends.
- **Update** that flips ownership to the target Queue -> sends.
- **Update** that does not change owner -> does not send (entry condition).
- **No email on the record** -> guard exits cleanly.

## Deploy

```bash
sf project deploy start \
  --source-dir force-app/main/default/letterhead \
  --source-dir force-app/main/default/email \
  --source-dir force-app/main/default/flows/<Object>_<Trigger>.flow-meta.xml \
  --target-org <alias>
```

Deploy the letterhead first (the email template references it), then the email folder + template, then the flow.

## QA

- **MT-01:** Create a record assigned to the target Queue with an email address — confirm the email is received.
- **MT-02:** Create a record assigned elsewhere — confirm no email.
- **MT-03:** Update a record's owner to the target Queue — confirm the email is sent.
- **MT-04:** Update a record's owner to the target Queue when `Email` is blank — confirm no email and no error.

# Skill: Flow deployment strategy

## Purpose

Reduce deployment failures caused by Flow ordering, activation state, and environment-specific dependencies.

## Conventions

- Keep Flow API names stable and version intentionally (do not rename to "fix" minor changes).
- Avoid referencing profiles directly when possible; prefer permission sets and custom permissions for entry conditions and visibility.
- Naming: `Object_When_What` (e.g. `Account_AfterSave_Health_Sync`).

## Deployment approach

- Deploy **dependent metadata first** (objects / fields / record types / picklist values).
- Deploy Flows **inactive** when activation can fail due to missing runtime dependencies; activate as a controlled post-deploy step.
- For **screen flows** referenced by **quick actions**, deploy the flow **before** the quick action (the quick action references the flow API name).
- For **before-save flows** that reference a custom field, deploy the field first.
- Screen Flow gotcha: the first screen must have at least one of `allowBack=true` / `allowFinish=true`.

## Activation

- After deploy, confirm flows are **Active** in Setup -> Flows. Some pipelines deploy as inactive by default.
- Activation can be a separate post-deploy step in the runbook.

## Validation

- Validate with target business scenarios in a sandbox.
- Run regression smoke tests for any object whose record-trigger flows changed.
- For after-save flows that call invocable Apex (e.g. assignment-rule re-execution), confirm the Apex class is deployed and the Flow's action input mapping resolves to the right `@InvocableVariable`.

# Skill: Lead Conversion

Patterns for persisting Lead identity, mapping custom fields onto Account / Contact / Opportunity, and gating conversion eligibility.

## Pattern A — Persist the Lead Id on the converted Opportunity

Useful when an external system (data warehouse, BI) needs to join converted records back to the originating Lead.

### Why a formula field on Lead?

The Lead's standard `Id` cannot be used directly as a source in `LeadConvertSettings` mapping — the mapping requires a **custom field** as the source. A formula field solves this:

| Object | Field | Type | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Lead` | `Lead_ID_Custom__c` | Formula (Text) | `CASESAFEID(Id)` — always 18-character, case-safe, auto-computed |
| `Opportunity` (or Account / Contact) | `Lead_ID__c` | Text(18) | Receives the value during conversion; `null` for non-converted records |

### Why a Text field (not Lookup or Formula) on the destination?

1. It receives the string value from the formula during conversion.
2. It must remain `null` for records created without lead conversion (a Lookup or Formula would not satisfy this).
3. Downstream consumers use it as a string join key; no Salesforce relationship semantics are needed.

### `LeadConvertSettings` mapping

```xml
<objectMapping>
    <inputObject>Lead</inputObject>
    <outputObject>Opportunity</outputObject>
    <mappingFields>
        <inputField>Lead_ID_Custom__c</inputField>
        <outputField>Lead_ID__c</outputField>
    </mappingFields>
</objectMapping>
```

### FLS

- Source formula field on Lead: read-only by definition (formulas are not editable). Grant **Read** to the personas that need traceability.
- Destination text field on Opportunity / Account / Contact: **Read + Edit** to admin / integration users; **Hidden** from end users if it is purely an integration field.

### Page layouts

If the field is purely for integration, **exclude it from all page layouts**. Otherwise add it to the System Information section.

### Deployment order

1. Deploy the Lead formula field (`Lead_ID_Custom__c`).
2. Deploy the destination Text field (`Lead_ID__c`).
3. Deploy `LeadConvertSettings` (mapping depends on both fields existing).
4. Deploy profile / permission set FLS.
5. Deploy Apex tests.

### QA

- **AT-01:** Convert a Lead — assert the destination field equals `CASESAFEID(Lead.Id)` (18 chars).
- **AT-02:** Create the destination record without conversion — assert the field is `null`.
- **AT-03:** Query as a non-privileged user (`System.runAs`) — assert FLS denies read.

## Pattern B — Map a custom field on Lead to a custom field on the converted record

Same `LeadConvertSettings` mechanism. Both source (custom field on Lead) and destination (matching-type custom field on Account / Contact / Opportunity) must exist before deploying the mapping.

## Pattern C — Set the converted Opportunity's record type and close date from a Custom Metadata Type

For projects that convert leads into different Opportunity record types based on a key from the Lead (product, segment, region, etc.).

### Schema (suggested — adapt to your project)

`<Source_Key_To_Record_Type>__mdt`:

| Field | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Source_Key__c` | Text | Source value used to key the mapping (e.g. a `Product2.Type` value) |
| `Opportunity_Record_Type_Developer_Name__c` | Text (required) | Target Opportunity record type developer name |
| `Close_Date_Offset_Months__c` | Number (required) | Months to add to `Date.today()` for `CloseDate` |

### Apex (in `OpportunityTriggerHandler.beforeInsert`)

1. Load the CMT mappings into a `Map<String, <Cmt>__mdt>` keyed by source value.
2. For converted Opportunities (identified by a populated Lead-Id field, e.g. `Lead_ID__c`) with a populated source-key field (e.g. a `<Source_Key__c>` lookup):
   - Read the source key value (or look it up via the related record).
   - Look up the mapping; set `RecordTypeId` to the matching record type and `CloseDate = Date.today().addMonths(offset)`.
3. Bulk-safe: query related records, record types, and CMT once outside the loop.

## Pattern D — Conversion eligibility guard

Use a CMT-driven configurable rule engine (see `.cursor/skills/Custom_Metadata_Driven_Config.md`) so admins can change the rules without a deploy:

- Rule developer name: e.g. `Lead_Conversion`.
- Conditions reference `Account.Status__c != Inactive`, `Contact.Status__c != Inactive`, etc.
- Apex `LeadConversionEvaluator` exposes `@AuraEnabled` (for an LWC banner on the Lead record page) and `@InvocableMethod` (for a Flow).
- A `LeadTrigger` -> `LeadConversionGuard` runs in `before update`: when `IsConverted` flips to `true` and the rule evaluates `false`, `addError` to block conversion with a user-friendly message.
- The LWC banner on the Lead record page calls the same evaluator so the user sees the warning before clicking **Convert**.

## Pattern E — Re-run assignment rules after in-line edits

If your project assigns Leads on insert via assignment rules and you also want re-assignment after certain in-line edits:

- See `.cursor/skills/Assignment_Rule_Reexecution.md`.

# Skill: Profile and Permission Set patterns

Hard-won patterns for managing profiles, permission sets, permission set groups, and app visibility from source.

## Hierarchy and what lives where

| Container | Contains | Does **not** contain |
|---|---|---|
| Profile | Object permissions, FLS, app visibility, tab visibility, page-layout assignment, user permissions, record type visibility | Permission set group membership |
| Permission Set | Object permissions, FLS, app visibility, tab visibility, user permissions, custom permissions, record type visibility | Profile assignment |
| Permission Set Group | Member permission sets only | `<objectPermissions>` (object access lives on the member sets) |
| Custom Permission | A named flag the running user either has or does not have | Any actual privilege on its own (your code / config consumes it) |

## App Launcher visibility (very common pitfall)

A custom application appears in the App Launcher only when **every relevant profile** sets `<applicationVisibilities>` `visible=true` for that app.

```xml
<applicationVisibilities>
    <application>My_Custom_App</application>
    <default>false</default>
    <visible>true</visible>
</applicationVisibilities>
```

### Pitfalls

- A minimal profile file (only the new field / app entries) deployed over the org default can silently set `visible=false` or wipe other settings. **Retrieve the full profile first**, especially `Admin`, then edit and deploy.
- The **System Administrator** profile is large; deploying a partial Admin profile is a common cause of "the app exists but does not appear in the launcher."

### Recipe

```bash
sf project retrieve start --metadata Profile:Admin --target-org <alias>
# edit force-app/main/default/profiles/Admin.profile-meta.xml — add the applicationVisibilities block
sf project deploy start --source-dir force-app/main/default/profiles/Admin.profile-meta.xml --target-org <alias>
```

## CustomApplication + UtilityBar FlexiPage

The app's `<utilityBar>` value references a FlexiPage developer name; both must deploy together.

```xml
<!-- My_Custom_App.app-meta.xml -->
<utilityBar>My_Custom_App_UtilityBar</utilityBar>

<!-- My_Custom_App_UtilityBar.flexipage-meta.xml -->
<FlexiPage ...>
    <type>UtilityBar</type>
    <flexiPageRegions>
        <name>utilityItems</name>
        <type>Region</type>
        <itemInstances>
            <componentInstance>
                <componentName>notes:utilityBarNoteList</componentName>
            </componentInstance>
            <componentInstance>
                <componentName>runtime_sales_todo_list:unifiedToDoListAuraWrapper</componentName>
            </componentInstance>
        </flexiPageRegions>
    </itemInstances>
</FlexiPage>
```

Deploy both source files in the same command (or a single manifest).

## Salesforce permission dependencies

Salesforce enforces prerequisite chains. Common ones:

- **Modify All** on an object implies **Delete** and **View All** on that object.
- **`ManageUsers`** requires **`DelegatedTwoFactor`** and **`MonitorLoginHistory`**.
- **`ViewAllData`** has a long chain of dependent system permissions.
- Some permissions (e.g. `AllowForecasting`, `ExportReports`) are **not accepted as `<userPermissions>`** in some orgs; they must be granted in Setup or via the corresponding feature license.

### Recipe

When generating permission sets from a spreadsheet (Y/N grids), apply a **dependency normalization** pass after merging cells: walk a known table of "if granted X, also grant Y, Z" and add the implied permissions, otherwise the deploy fails with `unknown user permission` or `permission requires <other>`.

## Permission Set Group

```xml
<!-- My_Persona.permissionsetgroup-meta.xml -->
<PermissionSetGroup ...>
    <description>Persona X — combined permissions</description>
    <label>My Persona</label>
    <permissionSets>My_Persona_Object_Access</permissionSets>
    <permissionSets>My_Persona_System_Access</permissionSets>
</PermissionSetGroup>
```

Object permissions go on the member sets, not the group.

## Naming conventions

| Component | Convention |
|---|---|
| Permission set (object access) | `<Persona>_Object_Access` |
| Permission set (system / tabs / user perms) | `<Persona>_System_Access` or `<Default>_Access_for_<Persona>` |
| Permission set group | `<Persona>` |
| Custom application | `<Org>_<Function>` (e.g. `My_Sales`) |
| Utility bar FlexiPage | `<App>_UtilityBar` |
| Custom permission (bypass) | `<Object>_<Action>_Bypass` |

## Deployment order

1. Custom Permissions.
2. Permission Sets.
3. Permission Set Groups.
4. Profiles (can be combined with step 2 if your pipeline deploys the whole tree).
5. Custom Applications + their UtilityBar FlexiPages (together).
6. After deploy, assign the relevant permission set groups to users in Setup (or via a separate `sf data import` / data step).

## Page layout assignment after deploy

Salesforce often defaults new record types to the master layout for any profile that wasn't included in the metadata change. After deploy, walk **Setup -> Object Manager -> <Object> -> Page Layout Assignment** and confirm each profile uses the intended layout. Note this in the runbook.

# Skill: Quick Action launching a Screen Flow

A clean way to deliver a guided record action (Accept / Reject, Approve, Resolve, Submit-with-reason) without writing Apex.

## Anatomy

| Component | File | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Screen Flow | `flows/<Object>_<Action>.flow-meta.xml` | The guided UI: input `recordId`, screens, decisions, record updates, success message |
| Quick Action | `quickActions/<Object>.<Action>.quickAction-meta.xml` | The button users click; references the flow by API name |
| Page Layout | `layouts/<Object>-<Layout>.layout-meta.xml` | `platformActionList` includes `<Object>.<Action>` (qualified name) |
| FlexiPage (record page) | `flexipages/<Object>_Record_Page_*.flexipage-meta.xml` | Highlights panel `actionInstance` with visibility filters |

## Screen Flow skeleton

- **Type:** Screen Flow.
- **Inputs:** `recordId` (`Input` available, type matches the object).
- **First screen:** `allowBack=true` or `allowFinish=true` (Salesforce requires at least one).
- **Logic:** Screens, decisions, record updates as needed.
- **Output / success:** A final screen with success text, or close after a `Update Records` step.

## Quick Action skeleton

```xml
<QuickAction ...>
    <flowDefinition>My_Object_Reject</flowDefinition>
    <label>Reject</label>
    <name>Reject</name>
    <optionsCreateFeedItem>false</optionsCreateFeedItem>
    <type>Flow</type>
</QuickAction>
```

File name: `quickActions/MyObject.Reject.quickAction-meta.xml`.

## Page Layout: include the action

```xml
<platformActionList>
    <actionListContext>Record</actionListContext>
    <platformActionListItems>
        <actionName>MyObject.Reject</actionName>
        <actionType>QuickAction</actionType>
        <sortOrder>0</sortOrder>
    </platformActionListItems>
    <!-- ... other actions ... -->
</platformActionList>
```

Add to **every** layout where the action should appear (one per record type, typically).

## FlexiPage highlights panel: surface the action

In the Highlights Panel of the Lightning record page, add an `actionInstance` per action with visibility filters so it only appears in the right state. See `.cursor/skills/Dynamic_Forms_Field_Visibility.md` Pattern D.

```xml
<actionInstance>
    <actionName>MyObject.Reject</actionName>
    <visibilityRule>
        <criteria>
            <leftValue>{!Record.Status__c}</leftValue>
            <operator>EQUAL</operator>
            <rightValue>Pending</rightValue>
        </criteria>
    </visibilityRule>
</actionInstance>
```

Set `numVisibleActions` on the highlights panel to a number that fits all conditional actions.

## Common pitfalls

- **Flow not found at runtime:** the quick action references the flow API name; deploy the flow before the quick action.
- **Action not visible in the highlights panel:** the FlexiPage's `actionInstance` is missing or filtered out. Check the visibility rule.
- **Action not visible in the action bar (Salesforce Mobile / cards):** the page **layout's** `platformActionList` is missing the qualified `Object.Action` entry.
- **`enablePageActionConfig=true`:** requires Dynamic Actions for the object to be enabled in Setup; default to `false` unless confirmed.
- **FLS on fields the flow updates:** users running the action need edit on those fields. Add to the persona's permission set / profile FLS in the same change.

# Skill: UI Framework (Domain Knowledge)

Use this when building or reviewing Lightning UI.

## Expertise areas

- **LWC:** Lightning Web Components, wire adapters, Lightning Data Service (LDS), lifecycle hooks.
- **Aura:** Legacy support when required (components, events).
- **Lightning Messaging Service (LMS):** Cross-tab and cross-component communication.
- **SLDS:** Salesforce Lightning Design System — markup, tokens, accessibility.
- **Dynamic Forms / FlexiPages:** Field sections, header regions, visibility filters, `uiBehavior`.
- **Quick Actions:** Object-specific, screen-flow-launching, header actions.

## Key patterns

- Prefer LDS (`getRecord`, `updateRecord`, etc.) over custom Apex wire when CRUD is the only need.
- Use SLDS classes and structure; avoid one-off CSS that diverges from the design system.
- For LWC tests: Jest with standard LWC test utilities and wire mocks.
- Quick actions in `platformActionList` use the qualified `Object.ActionName` form.
- Screen Flows: the first screen must have `allowBack=true` or `allowFinish=true` (Salesforce requires it).
- `enablePageActionConfig=true` on a FlexiPage requires Dynamic Actions for the object to be enabled in Setup; do not flip it without confirming the org allows it.

## Common LWC scaffolding (per component)

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `<name>.html` | SLDS markup; no inline styles |
| `<name>.js` | Logic; wire adapters; LDS imports |
| `<name>.css` | Component-scoped styles only |
| `<name>.js-meta.xml` | `<isExposed>`, target page types, design properties |
| `__tests__/<name>.test.js` | Jest tests with `@salesforce/sfdx-lwc-jest` |

## Accessibility checklist

- [ ] Every interactive element has a label (visible or `aria-label`).
- [ ] Keyboard navigation works (Tab order, Enter / Space activation).
- [ ] Color contrast meets WCAG AA via SLDS tokens.
- [ ] No text-only state (use icons + text together).

# Skill: Validation Rule Patterns

Reusable validation-rule formulas and conventions distilled from real Sales / Service Cloud projects. Use this skill whenever a story asks for "must be filled when ...", "must follow format ...", or "cannot change after ...".

## Authoring rules

1. **One purpose per rule.** Combine multiple acceptance criteria in one rule **only** when they share the same activation context and the same error message would make sense.
2. **Name** the rule for what it enforces, not the AC number: `Field_Required_When_Stage`, `Format_Email_Lead`, `Block_Edit_Closed_Opportunity`.
3. **`errorDisplayField`:** when the rule targets a single field, attach the error to that field (e.g. `Email`); use top-of-page only for cross-field rules.
4. Always paraphrase the error message so a user knows **what to fix** (not just "invalid input").
5. Add a manual test case (`MT-NN`) to the story's `qa-test-request.md` for every new validation rule.

## Pattern 1 — Required field when status / stage transitions

```
AND(
    ISPICKVAL(StageName, "<TargetStageOrStatus>"),
    ISBLANK(<RequiredField__c>)
)
```

For text values inside a picklist field, wrap with `TEXT(...)`:

```
AND(
    ISPICKVAL(StageName, "<TargetStage>"),
    ISBLANK(TEXT(<PicklistField__c>))
)
```

When more than one field is required, prefer narrow rules per field (or one rule with `OR(ISBLANK(...), ISBLANK(...))` and an error message that lists every missing field).

## Pattern 2 — At least one of N must be filled

```
AND(
    ISBLANK(<FieldA>),
    ISBLANK(<FieldB>),
    ISBLANK(<FieldC>)
)
```

Error message: "At least one of A, B, or C is required."

## Pattern 3 — Cross-field "if A then B"

Marketing-rejection style: the field A is allowed to satisfy a downstream rule when its sibling B is blank.

```
AND(
    ISPICKVAL(<Status>, "Cancelled"),
    ISBLANK(TEXT(<Closed_Reason__c>)),
    ISBLANK(<Rejection_Reason__c>)     /* allow either reason field to satisfy the rule */
)
```

## Pattern 4 — Email format

```
AND(
    NOT(ISBLANK(Email)),
    OR(
        CONTAINS(Email, " "),
        NOT(REGEX(Email, ".+@.+\\..+"))
    )
)
```

REGEX `.+@.+\\..+` requires `user@domain.tld` minimum. Document the intent in the design note.

## Pattern 5 — Phone / mobile format hardening

Catches unmatched parentheses, leading / trailing hyphens, double spaces, consecutive hyphens, hyphen-adjacent spaces, and "all the same digit" numbers (e.g. `9999999999`).

```
AND(NOT(ISBLANK(Phone)),
    OR(
        /* unmatched parentheses: count '(' vs ')' */
        (LEN(Phone) - LEN(SUBSTITUTE(Phone,"(","")))
            != (LEN(Phone) - LEN(SUBSTITUTE(Phone,")",""))),
        LEFT(TRIM(Phone), 1) = "-",
        RIGHT(TRIM(Phone), 1) = "-",
        CONTAINS(Phone, "  "),
        CONTAINS(Phone, "--"),
        CONTAINS(Phone, " -"),
        CONTAINS(Phone, "- "),
        REGEX(
            SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(
            SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(
                Phone," ",""),"-",""),"(",""),")",""),"+",""),".",""),
            "(\\d)\\1{9,}"
        )
    )
)
```

`(\\d)\\1{9,}` after stripping formatting catches 10+ consecutive identical digits.

## Pattern 6 — Name format (FirstName / LastName)

`FirstName` is part of a standard compound name and **cannot be set required via metadata** — enforce required + format via a validation rule:

```
OR(
    ISBLANK(FirstName),
    AND(NOT(ISBLANK(FirstName)),
        OR(
            LEN(TRIM(FirstName)) = 1,
            REGEX(FirstName, ".*[0-9].*"),         /* contains digits */
            NOT(REGEX(FirstName, ".*[a-zA-Z].*")), /* only special chars */
            CONTAINS(FirstName, "..")
        )
    )
)
```

## Pattern 7 — Block edits after a status / stage is reached

When a user must not change fields once the record is "closed" (or any terminal status), do this in **Apex** rather than a validation rule (you need to compare each populated field against its prior value). The Apex pattern lives in `.cursor/skills/Bypass_Patterns.md` and the `Apex_Architect` agent.

A pure-formula version that blocks **any** change while a status is set:

```
AND(
    PRIORVALUE(IsClosed) = true,
    NOT(ISCHANGED(IsClosed))   /* still closed; not just being closed/reopened */
)
```

This tells you the record was already closed and stays closed; pair with a check on a specific field if you want to allow some fields to remain editable. For the full "edit any updateable field" enforcement, prefer the Apex trigger handler pattern.

## Pattern 8 — Standard field that must keep a value (read-only via FLS)

For fields like `Probability` that must not be edited by certain personas, prefer **profile / permission set FLS** (`editable=false`, `readable=true`) over a validation rule. Keep the rule for cross-field invariants only.
